cards.title: Which law, and where
cards.body: The RED is Directive 2014/53/EU, applied from 13 June 2016, in the EU, in Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway, and in Türkiye. The UK has been a third country since 1 February 2020. The EU declaration states EU legislation. Other countries' declarations sit beside it, not inside it.

cards.title: What a radio is
cards.body: Radio equipment intentionally emits or receives radio waves for communication or radiodetermination, or it needs an accessory such as an antenna to do that. Radio waves here are below 3 000 GHz with no artificial guide. NFC is in that idea. Placing on the market is the first making-available of each unit.

cards.title: Not everything is in scope
cards.body: Exclusive public-security equipment can be out. Dual-use that is also sold for civil use is in. Amateur kits built for amateurs can be out. SOLAS marine equipment is under the marine directive. Ground aviation radio is generally in. A custom evaluation kit is out only if every element of that exemption is true.

cards.title: Article 3, and the other directives
cards.body: Article 3.1(a) is safety and health, 3.1(b) is EMC, 3.2 is spectrum, 3.3 is the extra requirements when they are switched on, and 3.4 is the common charger. Radio in the RED is excluded from the LVD and the EMCD. The RED points back at their essential requirements instead of a second file for the same EMC duty.

cards.title: Standards and modules
cards.body: A harmonised standard cited in the Official Journal gives a presumption of conformity for what it covers. Using one is optional. Module A needs no notified body and remains available for 3.1(a), 3.1(b), and 3.4. For 3.2 and 3.3, skipping or only partly using the harmonised standard means Module B+C or Module H, with a notified body.

cards.title: The manufacturer's list
cards.body: Design to Article 3, do the assessment, make sure the radio can operate in at least one Member State, keep the technical file, draw up the declaration, affix CE, identify the unit, put name and address on the product, and ship instructions with bands and power. Series production has to stay in conformity. The file is kept 10 years.

cards.title: Who else is on the hook
cards.body: An authorised representative in the EU cannot take over the design duty, the assessment, or the drafting of the technical file. An importer keeps a copy of the declaration for 10 years and must be able to produce the file, without having to store the file. A distributor checks CE, instructions, and traceability before selling.

cards.title: EN 301 489-1
cards.body: V2.2.3 is an EMC standard for radio and ancillary equipment under Article 3.1(b), not for broadcast receivers, and not a substitute for the Article 3.2 radio test of the enclosure and the antenna port. Ancillary enclosure emissions, tested apart, use EN 55032 Class B, or Class A only for exclusive industrial or telecom-centre use.

cards.title: Two performance rules
cards.body: Continuous phenomena, including the 3 V/m field from 80 MHz to 6 GHz: keep operating, do not transmit by mistake, do not change state, do not change critical data. Transients, including ±4 kV contact and ±8 kV air: no mode change and no loss of critical data, and the radio works again afterwards. ESD is not applied to vehicle use in Table 2.

cards.title: CE plus CE is not CE
cards.body: REDCA TGN 01: a certified module plus a CE-marked host is a new final radio product. Module EMC and safety results do not carry the final product. The module's EU-type certificate is not the final product's certificate. Installation instructions should say that the final product still needs its own Article 3 assessment.
